name: pipeline
description: A CSV data pipeline: import, row validation and cleaning, per-group aggregation, an on-disk JSON cache and export to SQLite or CSV.
author: test-split author (agent, written without reading the reviewer)

issues.description: The docstring says problems go to a new list when none is passed, but the default list is created once and shared, so every call without a list (every pipeline run) keeps the errors of all earlier calls.
issues.fix_hint: Default to None and create a new list inside the function.

issues.description: Amounts are documented to round half cents away from zero ("0.125" gives 0.13), but round() rounds halves to even, so 0.125 becomes 0.12 and 0.625 becomes 0.62.
issues.fix_hint: Quantize a Decimal of the amount to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP.

issues.description: Placeholders such as NA, N/A and NULL are supposed to count as missing whatever their case, but the value is compared with the lower-case marker set without lower-casing it, so "NA" or "NULL" pass as real values.

Cache keys start with the job's dataset name, which comes from whoever submitted the job, and are joined into a file path unchecked; a name such as ../../x makes put write (and get read) files outside the cache folder.
issues.fix_hint: Resolve the path and refuse keys whose file would not sit directly in the cache folder (or map keys to safe file names).

issues.description: The low-level cache imports the orchestrating runner just to read PIPELINE_VERSION while runner imports cache; the cycle only works because pipeline/__init__ happens to import runner first.
read_csv_text repeats the whole parsing loop of read_csv instead of both sharing one helper that takes a reader.
_strip_currency is never called; parse_amount strips symbols with its own translate table.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: Only the constant column names and the right number of ? placeholders are formatted into the statement; every value, the dataset name included, is bound as a parameter.
MD5 is used only as a change-detection checksum of a local file, not for anything security related, and is marked usedforsecurity=False.
